statement: For every d≥3, the number of degree-d plane curves of genus (d−1)(d−2)/2−1 through d(d+3)/2−1 generic points equals 3(d−1)². This is the degree of the discriminant hypersurface of singular degree-d curves, so a generic pencil has 3(d−1)² singular members.

answer.text: For every d≥3, the number of degree-d plane curves of genus (d−1)(d−2)/2−1 through d(d+3)/2−1 generic points equals 3(d−1)². This is the degree of the discriminant hypersurface of singular degree-d curves, so a generic pencil has 3(d−1)² singular members.

notes:
A new proof of a classical formula; generic singular members have one node.

Imported from the 2026-10-26 catalogue record R_9b8717d32d7252bb; the source claim has not been newly rechecked against the paper for this beta import.

The degree3(d−1)^2 is the classical homogeneous-discriminant formula attributed to Boole (GKZ, Chapter 1 Example 4.15 and Chapter 9 Example 1.6). Brugallé–Mikhalkin give a later floor-diagram verification. For monodromy records, this supplies only the discriminant degree/irreducibility; the separate sectional-monodromy argument supplies the group.
scope: Projective plane curves of degree d≥3; discriminant in their coefficient space, equivalently singular members of a generic pencil.
